---
title: "Week 5: Algorithmic Accountability, Bias, and Political Geography"
---

## Theme

Predictive risk models now influence who gets flagged for child welfare
investigation, who is triaged first in an emergency department, and who
qualifies for housing assistance. Crucially, these algorithms are built
on data that is itself shaped by political decisions --- including
redistricting, which determines who votes in which district and thus
which communities get political representation and public investment.
This week we examine algorithmic bias in public health AND explore how
redistricting data can reveal political geographies of health inequity.

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Due process and algorithmic decision-making in
government; disparate impact doctrine under Title VI and the Civil
Rights Act; the Voting Rights Act and redistricting as a legal framework
for political representation; prison gerrymandering.

**Health Focus:** How political geography (district boundaries) shapes
public health investment; whether communities with high health burden
are systematically gerrymandered out of political representation; the
connection between algorithmic bias in public health systems and
structural racism.

**Data:** Redistricting Data Hub, Ohio state page
(redistrictingdatahub.org/data/ohio): 2020 Census Block PL 94-171 data;
2023 ACS Poverty and Race data at the census tract level; 2024 General
Election Precinct-Level Results; Approved 2025 Congressional Districts.
All free downloads after free account registration.

**R Code:** Download shapefiles from Redistricting Data Hub; load with
sf::st_read(); join ACS poverty and race data by GEOID; map
congressional district boundaries overlaid on health outcome data
(PLACES) or SVI; compute summary statistics of health burden by
congressional district.

- Download the 2025 Approved Ohio Congressional District boundaries
  shapefile from Redistricting Data Hub
  (redistrictingdatahub.org/data/ohio)

- Download the 2023 ACS Census Tract Race Data and Poverty Data for Ohio
  from Redistricting Data Hub

- Load both datasets in R using sf::st_read() and read_csv(); join by
  GEOID

- Perform a spatial join to assign each census tract to its
  congressional district using sf::st_join()

- Compute mean poverty rate and racial composition by congressional
  district; produce a bar chart comparing district-level poverty rates;
  identify which districts represent the highest-burden communities
